visuals.title: Long latency
visuals.text: Disease shows up decades after the job, so ask about work long ago.

visuals.text: Fibres lodge in the distal airways and migrate to the pleura.

glossary.Interstitial fibrosis: Scarring of the tissue between the air sacs, making the lungs stiff.
glossary.Fibrosis: Replacement of normal tissue with scar tissue.
glossary.Malignancy: Cancer: abnormal cells growing uncontrollably and able to spread.
glossary.Occupational exposure: Contact with a harmful substance through a person's job.
glossary.Latency period: The time between exposure to a cause and the disease appearing.
glossary.Reduced chest expansion: The chest moves less than normal on breathing in, as in stiff fibrotic lungs.
glossary.Percussion: Tapping the chest to hear whether the area beneath is air-filled, solid or fluid.
glossary.Hyperdense: Appearing brighter or whiter than surrounding tissue on CT.
glossary.Calcified: Hardened by deposits of calcium salts; shows white on X-ray.
glossary.Lower lobes: The bottom sections of each lung.
glossary.Lateral chest wall: The side of the chest, under the armpit.
glossary.Diaphragm: Dome-shaped muscle separating chest from abdomen; the main breathing muscle.
glossary.Consolidation: Lung air spaces filled with fluid, pus or cells, as in pneumonia.
glossary.Premalignant: Not cancer, but able to turn into cancer.
glossary.CT chest: Computed tomography scan giving cross-sectional images of the chest.
glossary.Lung function tests: Breathing tests measuring lung volumes, airflow and gas transfer.
glossary.Biopsy: Taking a small tissue sample for examination under a microscope.
glossary.Pleural biopsy: A tissue sample taken from the lining of the lung.
glossary.Smoking cessation: Stopping smoking, ideally with behavioural support and medication.
glossary.Oxygen therapy: Giving extra oxygen to correct low blood oxygen levels.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that relieves symptoms and maintains function rather than curing the disease.
glossary.Staging: Describing how far a cancer has grown or spread, to guide treatment.
glossary.Drainage: Removing fluid, here from the pleural space, using a needle or tube.
glossary.Distal airways: The smallest airways furthest from the trachea, near the alveoli.
glossary.Inflammatory mediators: Chemicals such as cytokines released by cells that drive inflammation.
glossary.Chronic inflammation: Long-lasting inflammation that damages tissue and causes scarring.
glossary.Mutation: A change in the DNA sequence of a cell.
glossary.Multiplicative risk: When two risks combine, the total is the product of them, not the sum.
glossary.Shipbuilding: Industry that historically used large amounts of asbestos insulation.
glossary.Insulation: Material used to stop heat loss; older lagging often contained asbestos.
